transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What has been bothering you or bringing you in?

I feel like I’ve lost all interest in teaching and the activities I used to enjoy, and I can’t seem to care about anything the way I used to. I finally decided to seek help after my principal suggested I take a personal day because some of my colleagues noticed I was really struggling.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life, or did they come on without a clear trigger? About how long have you been feeling this way?

It really started about two years ago when I took on a lot of extra teaching responsibilities, managed several clubs, and had to deal with a stressful new school evaluation system. This heavy, joyless feeling has been pretty constant and building for about a year and a half now.

Before this started about two years ago, had you ever had another period lasting at least two weeks when you felt similarly depressed or lost interest in things? Or is this the first time in your life you’ve had symptoms like this?
No, I don't recall ever feeling this way before all of this started. As far as I can remember, this is the first time in my life I have experienced these kinds of symptoms.

If your workload or school stress were reduced, do you think your mood would improve fairly quickly, or does the sadness and loss of interest now feel present most of the time regardless of what is happening? Are you also having other depression symptoms like changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, trouble concentrating, or feelings of worthlessness?

The joyless feeling is constant now and doesn't lift even when things go well at school. I'm also barely eating and losing weight, lying awake for hours with my mind spinning, and feeling constantly exhausted. On top of that, my brain feels too foggy to make simple decisions, and I constantly spiral into guilt, feeling like a failure who is letting everyone down.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming or killing yourself? If so, have you made any plans or taken any steps toward it?

Sometimes at night when I'm feeling really overwhelmed, I catch myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up or if I got into an accident. I don't have any plans or intentions to harm myself, but the idea of just not being here anymore sometimes feels like a relief.
When you feel most depressed, have you ever heard or seen things other people don’t, or become convinced of things like being unforgivably guilty or ruined even when others say that isn’t true?

No, I’ve never seen or heard things that others couldn't, and I don't think my thoughts have gone that far. While I do feel an intense amount of guilt and constantly worry that I'm failing everyone, I know those are just my own negative thoughts and not hallucinations or anything like that.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked faster than usual, or did things that felt out of character or risky? Even if it didn’t seem like a problem at the time, has anything like that ever happened?
No, I've never had any periods where I felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or hyperactive. In fact, I've mostly felt the complete opposite—just constantly drained and down.

How much is this depression affecting your day-to-day functioning—for example, are you still able to teach, manage basic tasks at home, and take care of yourself? Have you missed work or found yourself unable to do things you normally could?

It has completely derailed my life; I've started missing grading and documentation deadlines, which led to my principal checking in and suggesting that personal day. Outside of work, I've stopped seeing friends and let household tasks and our finances slide, which has caused a lot of tension with my husband. I've never allowed things to get this disorganized before, and I just feel like I'm failing at everything.
